# Tier `rockchip-rk3588`

## Serving

| setting | value | what it controls |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `rk3588` | which `llama-swap.*.yaml` template renders |
| ctx_size | 8192 | the served window (`--ctx-size`) |
| kv_type | `f16` | `--cache-type-k/v`, kept symmetric |
| flash_attn | `off` | `--flash-attn` (required for a q8_0 V cache) |
| resident_tier | `gemma4-e2b` | the model that stays hot; seeds the agent planner seat (agent_model) when it differs from the workhorse |
| agent_ctx_tokens | 8192 | the agent's `-ctx-tokens` compaction budget |
| 26B-A4B | dropped | whether the 26B MoE is served, and where its experts live |

## Agent seat

This tier declares no persistent vLLM agent seat: the agent lane runs on the
llama.cpp seat named by `agent_model` above, in the tier's own llama-swap config.

## Media

This tier serves these media **seats** — models in its own llama-swap config, rendered
at install time. Each seat also produces the harness config binding that routes to it, so a
binding can never name a seat that was not rendered:

| seat | kind | binds | model | residency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `qwen3.5-0.8b-npu` | rkllm | `vision_model` | `qwen3.5-0.8b_w8a8_rk3588.rkllm` | swappable |

An `rkllm` seat runs on the NPU through the Rockchip RKLLM runtime, not in llama.cpp. It is
started with its own window and a `cpu_mask` — the CPUs the runtime's host threads may use
(at least 3, the runtime refuses fewer than the SoC has NPU cores):

- `qwen3.5-0.8b-npu`: window 16384, `cpu_mask` `0x0f`, vision encoder `qwen3.5-0.8b_vision_rk3588.rknn`

A seat still needs its weights on the box — model downloads stay out-of-band, as with
every seed.

It ships no file-backed media seed, so `generate_image` / `generate_video` /
`generate_audio` / `run_graph` report `NOT CONFIGURED` until an operator binds them.

## Installer-seeded config (non-media)

These `config_seed` keys are applied to a FRESH harness config exactly like the media
seed, but they bind no media route — the agent/cascade seats and per-node knobs live
here so they are never mistaken for a media capability:

| key | value |
|---|---|
| `escalation_model` | `` |
| `fleet_agent_enabled` | `false` |
| `model` | `gemma4-e2b` |
| `reasoning_model` | `` |
| `triage_model` | `gemma4-e2b` |
| `uma_reserve_gib` | `3` |

## Operator notes

Recorded with the profile — several are measurements from real hardware,
including reasons a tempting change was deliberately not made.

> Rockchip RK3588 SoC board (reference: an Orange Pi 5, RK3588S): 4x Cortex-A55 (cpu0-3) + 4x Cortex-A76 (cpu4-7), 7.7 GiB LPDDR4X shared by CPU, GPU and NPU (no dedicated VRAM), a 3-core 6 TOPS NPU and a Mali-G610 MP4 GPU. The board also runs the operator's home-automation stack, which decides the shape of the tier: NO model runs on the CPU (ADR 0054 amendment: no alt_backends, no CPU seat in the template), uma_reserve_gib 3 holds RAM back for that stack (fleet-serve advertises MemTotal less the reserve as capacity and MemAvailable less it as free, about 4.7 GiB of inference budget), and every model unloads after five idle minutes (ttl 300). Detection reads the device tree's root compatible: `rockchip,rk3588` on the vendor 6.1 kernel (board token rockchip,rk3588s-orangepi-5), `rockchip,rk3588s` on mainline 7.0 (board token xunlong,orangepi-5); both boot entries must classify. Two accelerators serve models. (1) The Mali GPU through llama.cpp on the Vulkan backend, from this tier's OWN template (llama-swap.linux-rk3588.yaml): the stock vulkan template always renders offload-e4b (~5 GB plus KV), which does not fit this budget, so the template lists only models that fit, one chat entry today (gemma4-e2b). The vendor kernel exposes the GPU as mali_kbase with an OpenCL blob only; mainline uses panthor with Mesa 25.2.8 panvk (Vulkan 1.4 on 'Mali-G610'), so this entry needs the mainline kernel. (2) The NPU through the Rockchip RKLLM runtime (rkllm seat qwen3.5-0.8b-npu, a chat model and a VLM, served by accelerators/rknpu/rkllm_server.py). The NPU driver is built into the vendor kernel and is the out-of-tree rknpu 0.9.8 DKMS module on mainline; the in-tree rocket driver is a different stack and does not run the RKNN or RKLLM runtimes. Measured (RKLLM 1.3.1, Qwen3.5-0.8B W8A8, 16384 context, VmHWM 1,178 MB, one 1,256-token prompt, mainline 7.0 + rknpu 0.9.8): cpu_mask 0x0f (A55 x4) prefill 44.5 / decode 9.07 tok/s, 0xf0 (A76 x4) 174.5 / 16.67; on the vendor 6.1 kernel with rknpu 0.9.7: 0x0f 40.9 / 12.2, 0xe0 (A76 x3) 166.9 / 11.3, 0xf0 200.1 / 18.7. RKLLM refuses fewer enabled CPUs than the 3 NPU cores, so a cpu_mask needs at least three bits; the tier default is the A55 cluster 0x0f (strict CPU reservation) until the operator chooses otherwise. vLLM has no Mali or RKNPU target, so this tier declares no vllm_seat. NOT MEASURED: the GPU seat. gemma4-e2b through llama.cpp Vulkan on the Mali-G610 has no speed or quality figure yet, and ctx_size 8192, f16 KV and flash-attn off are conservative defaults, not measurements; an on-box benchmark decides the GPU model list. Also unmeasured: the GPU and NPU seats loaded together (they are alternatives in one matrix set), the VLM's answer quality, and any agent seat (fleet_agent_enabled is false and none has been chosen). PROJECTED until that benchmark.
